_source: awk run with sh -c in containers of these images (docker run -d, one docker exec per case as uid 0, a fresh /tmp/w per case, the locale of `locale` unless the case sets LC_ALL), 2026-10-21, Docker 29.8.2 on linux/arm64: user functions (recursion, a parameter shadowing a global, local parameters, an array by reference, an undefined function, reached and not), range patterns, rand() and srand() (in one run, in two runs, one second apart, the return value of srand), printf widths and conversions, large integers, the form of numbers in print, CONVFMT, length / substr / index / toupper of UTF-8 text with LC_ALL=C, C.UTF-8 and (Red Hat) en_US.UTF-8, index(s, "") and length() in BEGIN, a rule and END. awks: gawk 4.0.2 (centos:7), 4.1.4 (debian:9 with the gawk package of archive.debian.org), 5.1.0 (rockylinux:9), 5.2.1 (debian:12 with the gawk package), mawk 1.3.3 (debian:10), 1.3.4 20200120 (ubuntu:22.04), 20240123 (ubuntu:24.04), 20250131 (debian:13), BusyBox 1.36.1 (busybox:1.36.1-musl). Raw output, nothing normalised. Volatile (they carry the clock or the entropy of the run and differ in a second run; the tests compare their form only): every srand() without an argument and the value srand returns where it is the clock (gawk, BusyBox: the second srand() of `srand(); srand()`; mawk: every return value but an argument given before), rand() without srand in mawk 1.3.3, 20200120 and 20240123, srand(1) in mawk 20240123, CONVFMT="%d" in mawk 20240123. A second run of a sample of 74 cases gave the same output but for five of these. `meta` names each case, `groups.version` the version calls (not run by the tests).
